claims.text: The paper addresses interactive segmentation errors around fine details, small objects and complex boundaries, and refinement loops that distribute effort uniformly rather than targeting critical error regions.
The architecture uses a shared MAE-pretrained plain ViT with an FPN; positive and negative click disk maps are concatenated with the previous segmentation mask and embedded alongside image patches.

An auxiliary edge head receives supervision from edge maps generated from segmentation masks using differential operators such as Laplacian or Sobel filters; training combines normalized focal segmentation loss with Dice edge loss.
U-CFR computes predictive uncertainty as 1−|2Pseg−1| and multiplies it by the normalized Sobel gradient magnitude of the segmentation probability map to obtain boundary-aware uncertainty.

After each user interaction, U-CFR selects the maximum boundary-aware uncertainty location as a pseudo-click candidate. It skips candidates with probabilities in the inclusive interval [0.49, 0.51], assigns positive labels above 0.51 and negative labels below 0.49, then feeds accepted clicks back into the model.
Training uses SBD, reported as containing 8,498 training images and 2,820 test images. Evaluation includes SBD, COCO_MVal, Pascal VOC, DAVIS, Berkeley, GrabCut, BraTS, ssTEM and OAIZIB.
Out-of-domain evaluation uses BraTS, ssTEM, OAIZIB and a curated irradiated-metallic SEM precipitate dataset; models trained solely on SBD are applied without fine-tuning.
Adding the edge head reduces NoC@90 relative to SimpleClick from 2.81 to 2.70 on Pascal VOC, 4.07 to 3.90 on COCO_MVal and 5.24 to 5.01 on SBD.
On COCO_MVal, the edge-head model increases first-click mIoU from 61.03% to 66.05% and first-click NSDS from 0.29 to 0.31.
Compared with one-step CFR on the same base model, one-step U-CFR reduces NoC@90 from 2.72 to 2.64 on Pascal VOC, 3.88 to 3.80 on COCO_MVal and 4.98 to 4.94 on SBD.
Compared with SimpleClick, the full model reduces Berkeley NoC@90 from 2.46 to 2.19, reported as an 11% improvement, and NoC@95 from 6.71 to 6.07, reported as a 9.5% improvement.
On OAIZIB, the reported model reduces NoC@85 from SimpleClick's 18.44 to 16.68, increases first-click mIoU from 2.52% to 6.32%, and increases NSDS at 10 clicks from 0.58 to 0.72.
On SEM-Precipitate, the reported model requires 7.92 clicks for 85% IoU versus SimpleClick's 10.37 and achieves NSDS of 0.87 versus 0.81 at 10 clicks and 0.93 versus 0.89 at 20 clicks.
U-CFR does not improve every refinement metric: Table 2 reports lower mIoU at 10 clicks than CFR on Pascal VOC (97.80% versus 97.94%), COCO_MVal (94.92% versus 95.11%) and SBD (92.72% versus 92.85%).

The edge head is intended as a training-time regularizer rather than a geometrically precise standalone boundary detector; the paper notes that topology-aware losses could better capture thin-boundary connectivity.

The paper's stated contributions are an auxiliary edge-detection head for boundary-aware representations and an inference-time uncertainty-guided pseudo-click refinement framework that operates without additional user input.
